title: Fit the hose end into the tap's sprung-sleeve coupler so it holds when tugged
instruction: Attach the loose hose end to the coupler on the tap so that it cannot be pulled off, and leave it with nothing holding it.
context: Hooking a sprinkler, a soaker line or a car-wash brush to an outdoor tap often goes through a brass quick coupler, and landscaping and groundskeeping crews (about 1.2 million US workers) swap hoses between taps with them. A connector that is not fully home looks attached but blows off when the water is turned on.
setup: Simulation surrogate: Positions from the robot's view: 'in front' is the distance ahead of the line through the two arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the midline halfway between them, heights are above the table top. Tap (fixed): a garden standpipe tap, a chrome tap body (36 x 40 x 48 mm, red lever on top) on a grey steel post 32 x 32 mm with a 64 x 60 mm foot plate, its brass spout (21 mm across, 90 mm long with its adaptor) pointing to the robot's left. Coupler (brass, friction 0.3, fixed on the spout): its mouth is 30.0 cm in front and 1.0 cm right, facing left, the bore's axis 70 mm above the table and running left-right. A 28 x 28 mm front face with a 45-degree lead-in chamfer from 22 mm across down to a round 17.0 mm bore, 40 mm deep. Two steel locking pins (5 mm wide along the bore, 8 mm tall, round-nosed, 3 g each, 20 N/m springs) stand 2.0 mm into the bore from front and back, 9 mm behind the mouth; they can move 2.5 mm out. Collar: a round black anodised aluminium sleeve (39 mm across, 32 mm long, 50 g, knurled, friction 1.0) round the front, flush with the mouth, sprung forward (1.2 N at rest, 4.2 N at its 11 mm stop). Its inner land sits 0.3 mm outside the pins, so they cannot move out until the collar is pulled 6 mm or more toward the tap. Hose end (loose, 240 g, friction 0.5): a brass male hose connector (120 g): a 24 mm nose with a stepped tip (14, 15, then 16.0 mm across), a groove 6.4 mm wide with a 12.0 mm core from 6.2 to 12.6 mm in front of its flange, a 25 mm flange 6 mm thick and a 24 mm ferrule 34 mm long, on the last 48 cm of a green PVC garden hose 25 mm across (eight 60 mm sections of 15 g that bend). It lies straight on the table, the flange face's centre 27.0 cm in front and 15.0 cm left, 12.5 mm up, the nose pointing to the robot's right and 23 degrees away from the robot, the hose running back from it toward the robot's left. Nothing else is on the table. Real trials use Foster FHS4B manual straight-through socket and matching FH44FB unvalved plug, with the Dixon 5031208SS tap adapter, Parker 125HBL-12-8 hose barb and 480 mm of 19.05 mm-ID/25 mm-OD hose. Place the real socket mouth at the same declared coordinates and calibrate the visible stop/witness/home datums in README. The custom dimensions above are model parameters, not manufacturer dimensions.
scoring: Simulator: Measured along the coupler's bore: how far the flange face is from the mouth, the connector's offset from the axis and its angle to it. 0.25: at some moment the connector's nose was at least 14.5 mm into the bore, on the axis (within 2 mm and 6 degrees), past the locking pins. 0.5: at some moment it was home: flange within 2 mm of the mouth, within 1.5 mm and 5 degrees of the axis. 1.0 (locked): once it is home, the collar back within 1 mm of its forward stop, nothing touching it (no part of either arm within 5 mm of the hose end, the collar or the pins) and still for 1 s, the scorer pulls it straight out of the bore, rising from 1 N to 10 N over 0.5 s and held at 10 N for 0.5 s; it must come out at most 1.5 mm and be home and still afterwards, with nothing touching it. An unlocked connector is pulled out of the coupler (the pull stops once it has come 3 mm). Success (1.0) must hold 1 s. 0 if the hose end ends more than 2 cm below the table top (dropped off). Real trial: a spring scale attached to the rigid plug body or threaded adapter behind its shoulder, pulled along the bore; a rule on the bore for the depths. Real partial/home milestones use the calibrated visible W and H in README: W lies beyond the repeatable forward-sleeve obstruction; home is within 2 mm of H. Retention still requires the released 10 N axial test, no more than 1.5 mm outward movement and released/still success. The simulator 0.02 mm minimum-motion force diagnostic is not a real measurement requirement.
reset_notes: Simulator: 1. Pull the collar back toward the tap and hold it; pull the hose connector straight out; let the collar spring forward. 2. Check both pins stand 2.0 mm into the bore and the collar is flush with the mouth. 3. Lay the hose end straight on the table with the flange face's centre 27.0 cm in front and 15.0 cm left, nose pointing right and 23 degrees away from the robot. Nothing is consumed. Real hardware: isolate the tap, retract/hold the Foster FHS4B sleeve, withdraw FH44FB and release the sleeve. Check visible mating surfaces and spring return, verify the recorded stop/home references, remove the pull instrument and restore the photographed plug/hose start marks, far end free. Do not inspect simulated two-pin protrusions on the commercial socket.
fidelity: Full-size functional proxy for a manual sleeve-back hose coupling. Real trial: Foster FHS4B/FH44FB with the specified adapters. Simulation uses two pins for the product latch balls, a 12-sided bore/collar and eight hinged hose sections; its dimensions, mass, springs and friction are separate declared model parameters. No water pressure; the 10 N pull tests retention. Native results validate the unchanged proxy; commercial-hardware force and robot performance are unmeasured.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of 2 trials; in the first the arms went down near the hose end and the tap, in the second they stayed above the table, and neither grasped the hose end or the collar); demo: 1.0 in each of 2 trials (passed the 10 N pull test with nothing touching it)
